title: Coefficient description and ideal powers in a completed positive monoid algebra
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete and separated for the powers of $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $P$ be a commutative additive monoid generated by finitely many elements, embedded in a free abelian group $G\cong\mathbf Z^r$, and let $w:G	o\mathbf Z$ be a homomorphism strictly positive on $P\setminus\{0\}$. Put $A[P]= igoplus_{p\in P}Az^p$, with $z^pz^q=z^{p+q}$, $\mathfrak b=(\mathfrak m,z^p:p
e0)$ and $B=\varprojlim_n A[P]/\mathfrak b^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For $p\in P$, let $
u(p)$ be the largest integer $q$ for which $p=p_1+\cdots+p_q$ with all $p_i\in P\setminus\{0\}$; put $
u(0)=0$. This integer is finite. The natural coefficient map gives an isomorphism of $A$-algebras from $B$ to the ring of all families $(a_p)_{p\in P}\in A^P$, with componentwise addition and convolution multiplication $ (ab)_p=\sum_{u+v=p}a_ub_v$. Every sum in this formula is finite. The image of $az^p$ has coefficient $a$ at $p$ and zero elsewhere. For every integer $n\ge1$, the projection $\pi_n:B	o A[P]/\mathfrak b^n$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak b^nB$, and a family $(a_p)$ lies in this kernel exactly when $a_p\in\mathfrak m^{\max(n-
u(p),0)}$ for every $p\in P$. In particular, as $A$-modules, $B/\mathfrak b^nB\cong igoplus_{
u(p)<n} A/\mathfrak m^{n-
u(p)}$, with only finitely many summands.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-positive-monoid-adic-filtration] with $I=\mathfrak m$ and $J=\mathfrak b$. Its hypotheses are exactly finite generation of $P$, the embedding in $G$, and positivity of $w$. It supplies the attained $\nu$, finite decomposition sets and $S_n$, superadditivity of $\nu$, and the coefficient criterion for $\mathfrak b^n$ in $A[P]$.

source.place: Exposé VI §1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid models; not a verbatim theorem of ILO.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-filtered-monoid-coefficient-limit] with $I=\mathfrak m$, $R=A[P]$ and $J=\mathfrak b$. Step 1 supplies its superadditivity, finite $S_n$, finite pair decompositions and coefficient criterion; the given completeness and separatedness supplies its bijective coefficient-completion map. Its $\widehat R$ is $B$, with the same projections. It gives the $A$-algebra coefficient isomorphism, finite convolution and monomial formula, and $\pi_n(a)=[\sum_{p\in S_n}a_pz^p]$.

source.place: Exposé VI §1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid models; not a verbatim theorem of ILO.

proof.text: The truncation formula and the finite-level criterion show that $\ker\pi_n$ consists exactly of the families with $a_p\in\mathfrak m^{\max(n-\nu(p),0)}$: outside $S_n$ the condition is vacuous. The projection is onto since every polynomial class has the canonical compatible sequence of its images at every level. Also $\mathfrak b^nB\subseteq\ker\pi_n$, because $\pi_n$ kills the image of $\mathfrak b^n$.

source.place: Exposé VI §1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid models; not a verbatim theorem of ILO.

proof.text: Let $c:B\to A^P$ be the coefficient isomorphism and $\mathfrak j=(\mathfrak m z^0,z^p:p\ne0)$ in $A^P$. The monomial formula sends every generator of $\mathfrak b$ to the corresponding generator of $\mathfrak j$. Thus $c(\mathfrak b^nB)=\mathfrak j^n$: expand a finite sum of products of $n$ generators times arbitrary coefficients; applying $c$ gives one inclusion and applying $c^{-1}$ gives the other. Apply [lem-trf-finite-pattern-factorization] to a family in $c(\ker\pi_n)$, using step 3 and the given Noetherian locality, finite generation, finite-rank free $G$ and positive $w$. It belongs to $\mathfrak j^n$, so its inverse image belongs to $\mathfrak b^nB$. Together with step 3, this proves equality.

source.place: Exposé VI §1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid models; not a verbatim theorem of ILO.

proof.text: Send $x\in B$ to $(c(x)_p\bmod\mathfrak m^{n-\nu(p)})_{p\in S_n}$. This $A$-linear map has kernel $\mathfrak b^nB$ by steps 3--4, so its induced quotient map is injective. Given a tuple, lift its finitely many entries to $A$ and take the finite monomial sum. Its residue tuple is the original one by the monomial formula. Different lifts have differences in the displayed coefficient ideals, hence give the same class by steps 3--4. This gives an inverse to the quotient map: for any $x$, its difference from the chosen finite sum has zero residue tuple and is in the kernel. Finiteness of $S_n$ identifies these tuples with the asserted direct sum.

lean.statement: theorem monoidCompletion_coefficients (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A] (P : Type v) [AddCommMonoid P] [AddMonoid.FG P] (G : Type w) [AddCommGroup G] (ι : P →+ G) (hι : Function.Injective ι) (wgt : G →+ ℤ) (hpos : ∀ p : P, p ≠ 0 → 0 < wgt (ι p)) (hfree : ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (G ≃+ (Fin r → ℤ))) : ∃ (ν : P → ℕ), ν 0 = 0 ∧ (∀ p : P, IsGreatest {q : ℕ | ∃ p₁ : Fin q → P, (∀ i : Fin q, p₁ i ≠ 0) ∧ (∑ i, p₁ i) = p} (ν p)) ∧ ∃ (b : Ideal (AddMonoidAlgebra A P)), b = Ideal.map (algebraMap A (AddMonoidAlgebra A P)) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ⊔ Ideal.span {x | ∃ p : P, p ≠ 0 ∧ x = AddMonoidAlgebra.single p (1 : A)} ∧ ∃ (ring : CommRing (P → A)) (alg : @Algebra A (P → A) _ ring.toSemiring) (c : @AlgEquiv A (AdicCompletion b (AddMonoidAlgebra A P)) (P → A) _ _ ring.toSemiring _ alg), (∀ (a f : P → A) (p : P), (@Add.add (P → A) ring.toAdd a f) p = a p + f p) ∧ (∀ (a f : P → A) (p : P), (@Mul.mul (P → A) ring.toMul a f) p = ∑ᶠ q : {q : P × P // q.1 + q.2 = p}, a q.1.1 * f q.1.2) ∧ (∀ p : P, Set.Finite {q : P × P | q.1 + q.2 = p}) ∧ (∀ (a : A) (p q : P), c (AdicCompletion.of b (AddMonoidAlgebra A P) (AddMonoidAlgebra.single p a)) q = if q = p then a else 0) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → Set.Finite {p : P | ν p < n} ∧ Function.Surjective (AdicCompletion.evalₐ b n) ∧ RingHom.ker (AdicCompletion.evalₐ b n) = Ideal.map (algebraMap (AddMonoidAlgebra A P) (AdicCompletion b (AddMonoidAlgebra A P))) (b ^ n) ∧ (∀ x : AdicCompletion b (AddMonoidAlgebra A P), x ∈ RingHom.ker (AdicCompletion.evalₐ b n) ↔ ∀ p : P, c x p ∈ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ^ (n - ν p)) ∧ Nonempty ((AdicCompletion b (AddMonoidAlgebra A P) ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap (AddMonoidAlgebra A P) (AdicCompletion b (AddMonoidAlgebra A P))) (b ^ n)) ≃ₗ[A] ⨁ p : {p : P // ν p < n}, A ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) ^ (n - ν p.1)))
